text:
ivy: onboarding a Gemma-derived model (Eos9B) -> int4 run shows major QA drop on long docs, short queries OK.

jas: numbers + how did you quantize?

ivy: fp16 rougeL 44.2 / qa-f1 70.1. int4 -> rougeL 37.0 / qa-f1 62.4. tool: `model-tools convert --in eos9b.fp16 --out eos9b.int4 --method gptq --g=128`.

marc: repeating tokens or weird decodes?

ivy: yes, long traces have repeats and a few ZWJ/placeholder tokens in the tail. example: ids [50205,50206,50207] -> ["the","\u200b","the"].

jas: suspect rotary scaling mismatch (per-head vs shared) + tokenizer tail remap. convert assumes headwise by default?

ivy: default was headwise. upstream model metadata actually lists `rotary_mode: shared`. Oops.

marc: that mismatch will make per-head phases misalign; with quant noise it amplifies on long sequences. re-export or re-run convert with `--rotary-mode shared` and re-eval.

ivy: did that quickly: int4(shared) rougeL 42.3 / qa-f1 68.2. much better but still small delta.

jas: tokenizer issue remains. convert currently uses `vocab_len = len(tokens)` and slices positional/rotary tables assuming no extra sentinels. need `--tokenizer-path` and a safe remap step.

marc: add a tiny rotary probe during onboarding: compare mean L2 between tiled-shared and per-head rotary params to auto-detect mode. also add a tail-decoding smoke test for tokens in last 20 ids.

ivy: will patch convert + add probe and tests. opening a PR with a minimal probe and a sample failing trace.

ci-bot: pr/3391 opened by ivy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-tools/pull/3391 (tokenizer remap + rotary autodetect + tail-decoding test).

ivy: after PR and rerun, int4 rougeL 42.8 / qa-f1 68.8. long-ctx hallucinations down ~52%. closing for now.
